turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung's eyes narrowed in concern as he gazed at O-lan, his voice low and urgent, 'How can you think of these things, O-lan, when you are so weak and your body is so worn out?'

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung's fate was tied to the marriage of their son, O-lan thought, and she would not rest until it was settled before she was gone.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: What good is marriage if the woman is but a shadow of her former self, O-lan, and what is a son's future if his mother is not there to care for him?

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: The eldest son would be married, that was all that mattered, he must be settled before she was gone, no one else could care for him as she did.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son was calm, he reassured Wang Lung, and he would be just fine, the marriage arrangements would be made soon, and he would not forget the lessons O-lan had taught him, he would take good care of the family.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung's voice was stern, he scolded the eldest son, his eyes narrowing in suspicion, but his words betrayed a deeper concern, 'You think a few words will calm my heart, but I know what you are not saying, that you are troubled by your mother's illness, and it weighs on your mind, does it not?'}

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son's expression turned confident, he declared, 'Father, mother, do not worry, I will marry soon, and with a good family, one that will support us and care for us, just as O-lan has always done.'

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung was exasperated, he thought, O-lan must be out of her mind, must the arrangements be made now, can it not wait until she is stronger, until she is back on her feet?

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: No, Wang Lung, it cannot wait, she thought, the eldest son's future was all that mattered now, and she would not rest until it was settled

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: Wang Lung's eldest son was calm, he told O-lan, and he would take care of the arrangements, choosing a good family that would make her proud.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung's eyes narrowed, his voice low and stern, as he spoke of O-lan's preoccupation with their future, 'Foolish woman, you are still thinking of the future, but what of the present, what of your own life, are you not concerned for yourself, for your own well-being?'

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung, she thought, the eldest son's future was all that mattered, and she had given her life for this, to see him settled, to see him happy.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son was calm, his voice steady, as he reassured O-lan, 'You must not worry, I will find a good family, and they will make you proud, and I will take care of them, just as you have always taken care of us.'

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: But it is not just a marriage, Wang Lung, it is a good family, one that will take care of the eldest son, and make him happy

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son was worn out, he told O-lan, and he would speak to the matchmaker tomorrow, and they would find a good family for him to marry.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung, she must see the eldest son settled before she goes to the ancestors, it is the last thing she can do for him

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son was worried about his mother's health, but he tried to reassure her, telling her that he would be fine, and that she must take care of herself, eat well, and rest.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung's voice was low and firm, a growl that brooked no argument, as he spoke of finding a good family for their son, but he cautioned, 'We must not rush into this, we must think of what is best for our son, and for O-lan's peace of mind', his eyes locked on O-lan with a mix of concern and determination.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: The eldest son, he must be careful in choosing a family, one that will be kind to him, and treat him with respect, like a son of the family

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son nodded, his face set in a determined expression, and told his parents that he would go to the matchmaker early tomorrow, and would bring back several good families for them to consider.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
